title: GET /api/ibkr/status -- surface IBKR gateway connection state
description: app.api.dependencies.get_ibkr_provider exists and is already a thread-safe singleton (backend-ibkr-data-provider-followups), but nothing calls it -- the provider is fully dormant end-to-end. Add a read-only status endpoint wrapping IBKRProvider.get_gateway_status() so the app can actually surface 'IBKR: connected / not authenticated / gateway down / disabled' instead of this being invisible everywhere.

checklist.step: Add GET /api/ibkr/status returning the gateway state (available/gateway_unreachable/not_authenticated) plus an explicit 'disabled' state when Settings.ibkr_enabled is False, and a detail string.
Ensure the endpoint never raises for any gateway state -- degrade to the appropriate status value instead, matching IBKRProvider.get_gateway_status's own never-raises contract.
Unit tests mocking IBKRProvider for each of the four states (disabled, available, gateway_unreachable, not_authenticated).

decisions.decision: New GET /api/ibkr/status route lives in its own backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py (not appended to an existing router), registered in app/main.py alongside stocks/portfolio/watchlist. The handler derives 'disabled' purely from app.api.dependencies.get_ibkr_provider yielding None -- it does not separately call get_settings().ibkr_enabled -- since get_ibkr_provider's own documented contract is to yield None in exactly (and only) that case, so re-checking the flag directly would just be a redundant, potentially-divergent second source of truth for the same condition.
decisions.rationale: A dedicated router file matches this codebase's one-router-per-resource convention (stocks.py/portfolio.py/watchlist.py) rather than shoehorning an unrelated resource into watchlist.py or portfolio.py. Deriving 'disabled' from the dependency's own None sentinel (rather than re-reading Settings) keeps a single source of truth for 'is IBKR enabled' -- get_ibkr_provider.py's own docstring already commits to yielding None if and only if ibkr_enabled is False, so this endpoint just trusts that contract instead of duplicating the check.

decisions.decision: IBKRStatusResponse declares no `responses={...}` error cases beyond FastAPI's default (no 404/422/503 entries) -- the endpoint has no path/query parameters to fail validation on, and both get_gateway_status() and this handler are documented as never raising, so there is no genuine error case to declare per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard.
decisions.rationale: The API documentation standard's '404/422/503 etc.' requirement is for endpoints that actually have failure modes worth declaring to a client; forcing placeholder error responses onto a route that structurally cannot produce them would misrepresent the contract rather than clarify it.

comments.summary: IBKRStatusResponse.detail's schema description claims detail is "Always null for 'disabled'", but app/api/routers/ibkr.py's handler always populates a non-null explanatory string for that state (confirmed by backend/tests/integration/test_ibkr_status.py::test_status_disabled asserting `detail is not None`). Same wrong claim duplicated into backend/openapi.json, frontend/src/api/types.ts, and docs/architecture/API.md. Non-blocking (informational-only field, never required for a caller to branch on per the schema's own framing) -- tracked as backend-ibkr-status-endpoint-followups.

Verified the task-worker's claim that regenerating backend/openapi.json/frontend/src/api/types.ts picked up unrelated pre-existing docstring drift on GET /api/watchlist/breadth: confirmed main's backend/openapi.json already matched the current code docstring, but main's frontend/src/api/types.ts was stale (still had the old "No new provider calls result" text) -- this PR's regeneration step just caught types.ts up to what openapi.json already said. Description text only, no schema/type shape change -- genuinely in-scope snapshot catch-up, not a live behavior change.
